source: MAFF/GIZ, "Guidelines for Banana Export from Cambodia to China" (2022), section 1.1
text:
This guide frames China as a fast-growing, increasingly quality-conscious destination market for fresh fruit. As Chinese household income has risen substantially over the past decade, consumer demand has shifted toward higher-quality, traceable, and food-safety-certified fresh produce rather than the cheapest available option. China is described as one of the largest fresh fruit import markets in the world, sourcing from dozens of countries, with Southeast Asian tropical fruit exporters (including Thailand and Vietnam) among its largest suppliers.

Cambodia's own fruit exports to China have been growing off a small base, and the guide frames this growth as an opportunity that depends on Cambodia meeting China's increasingly strict phytosanitary and traceability requirements — the registration, packing-house, and quality-control requirements covered in the rest of this guide exist specifically because Chinese import authorities require them as a condition of market access, not as arbitrary paperwork.
